accepted.reason: SEIRS adds only one major mechanism (waning) beyond SEIR and keeps a simple observation map. However, for a single-season 31-week training window, the waning parameter is at risk of weak identifiability and may act as an over-flexible shape/peak-width adjuster rather than a well-supported process. Also, obs=I is not well aligned with the target (hospitalization rate) given the stated lag semantics; it can still be used as a baseline but is semantically mismatched.

rejected.reason: Observation-target alignment is better (delayed_I matches the stated hospitalization lag), but the proposal itself notes prior feedback that a 1-week delay degraded this series. With high peakiness and short training, adding both waning (SEIRS) and an explicit delay increases identifiability risk and can easily shift the peak too late, making this a higher-risk template to carry forward without stronger justification.

suggested_edits.edit: If keeping SEIRS, consider switching observation_map from 'I' to 'delayed_I' with delay_weeks=0 (i.e., use the delayed_I mapping without an added discrete lag) to improve hospitalization-rate semantic alignment while avoiding the extra peak-shift risk of a 1-week delay.

Clarify in the rationale that waning is included as a contingency but may be weakly identifiable in a single-season series; commit to constraining/regularizing waning during fitting (conceptually) to reduce over-flexibility, since fractional memory is not being used.
